transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... well, I guess I'm here because I've been having a little bit of trouble with... well, with my eating in the evenings. I hope it's okay that I came in for this. 

It's just... I try to be really good and strict all day at work, but then I get home and I don't know, I just end up eating a bit more than I meant to. Like, I'll have my regular dinner, but then I'll just keep going—some cereal, maybe crackers, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and some sweets... all within just a couple of hours. It's a little embarrassing to admit, to be honest. Does that make sense?
When you find yourself eating more than you intended in the evenings, does it feel like you can't stop or control what you're doing once you start?

Um... yes, actually. You put that really well. It's... well, it's a little hard to admit, because I feel like I should have more willpower, you know? But once I get started on those nights, it's like I just keep wandering back to the kitchen. 

Even while I'm literally telling myself in my head to stop, I just... I don't. I guess I don't really feel back in charge of what I'm doing until I'm just uncomfortably full. I hope that doesn't sound too awful... am I explaining that okay?
After these evening eating episodes, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, exercising a lot, or doing something else to try to balance out what you've eaten?

Oh, um... well, no, I definitely don't ever make myself sick. That sounds... really awful, and I would never want to do that. I try to be healthy about it, you know? 

I just... well, the next day, I try to make up for it in a good way. I'll usually just skip breakfast and lunch, just to balance things out, which seems pretty normal, right? Or I'll try to get some extra exercise in. Like, I might go for an extra-long hike, or if I have softball conditioning, I'll just push myself a little harder than usual... even if I'm feeling a bit tired. It's just my way of staying on track, I think. Does that seem like a reasonable way to handle it?
Do these evening eating episodes cause you a lot of distress, or do they interfere with your daily life in any way?

Oh, um... I wouldn't say it interferes too much. I really try not to let it get in the way of my actual life, you know? I'm definitely still keeping up with all my insurance clients, and my mentoring role at work, and all my responsibilities at home. I make sure all of that is taken care of, I promise. 

But... well, I guess it does cause a little bit of stress sometimes. Mostly just... if I have a public event coming up, I can get a bit distracted. I just start worrying about how my clothes are going to fit, and I guess I feel a little less confident than I should. I know it probably sounds a bit silly or vain to worry about my outfits like that at my age... I hope you don't think less of me for admitting it. It's just a small thing, really, and I still get my job done. Is it normal to feel that way?
Do these evening eating episodes usually start right after you wake up during the night or early in the morning, or do they typically happen while you're still awake and winding down in the evening?

Oh, no, I'm definitely awake. I don't wake up in the middle of the night to eat or anything like that. That sounds... well, a bit out of control, doesn't it? 

It's really just when I'm winding down for the night. You know, after I've finished all my work and gotten everything settled at home. It's just my time to relax, and I guess I just get a little carried away sometimes while I'm watching TV or reading. It's all while I'm still up and about for the evening. That's... that's the more normal way for these things to happen, right?
Can you tell me a bit more about how these evening eating episodes start? Do they usually happen all within a few hours, and do you feel like you're in control when you begin eating?

Oh, um... well, it does usually happen all within a couple of hours, yes. And when I start, I really do just intend to have a normal, small snack. Just a little treat after a long day of dealing with policies and clients, which I think is pretty standard. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... once I get started on those nights, it's like I just keep going back to the kitchen. Even while I'm actively telling myself to stop, I just keep grabbing a little more. I don't really feel back in charge of myself until I'm... well, until I'm uncomfortably full. 

It's really embarrassing to admit that out loud. I hope you don't think I have absolutely no willpower... I really am a very disciplined person in every other part of my life, I promise! It's just hard to stop once I'm in that mode. A lot of people struggle with losing track of their snacking when they're tired, don't they?

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms align more specifically with F50.2 (Binge eating disorder), as they describe loss of control during evening eating episodes, eating until uncomfortably full, and experiencing distress and compensatory behaviors such as fasting and excessive exercise. There is no evidence of self-induced vomiting or other purging behaviors, which would be more characteristic of F50.0 or F50.1. The eating episodes occur while fully awake and typically in the evening, ruling out F50.9 (Eating disorder, unspecified) as a primary diagnosis.
